name: Change a car tire
blurb: A twenty-minute roadside job that most drivers have never rehearsed. Doing it once in your own driveway is the difference between an inconvenience and a crisis.
gear: Your car’s jack, wrench and spare (find them now)
A high-vis vest, warning triangle and gloves
steps: Stop somewhere safe and level, engine off, handbrake on, hazards on, and everyone out of the car and behind a barrier.
Find the jacking points in your handbook. Jacking on the wrong part of the sill will bend the car.
Loosen the wheel nuts a half-turn while the wheel is still on the ground — otherwise the wheel just spins.
Jack until the tyre is just clear of the ground, remove the nuts, and swap the wheel.
Hand-tighten the nuts in a star pattern, lower the car, then torque them properly in the same star pattern.
Check the spare’s pressure, note any speed limit for a space-saver, and get the puncture repaired promptly.
tips: Never get under a car supported only by a jack.
Re-check the torque after 50 km. Nuts settle.
Do a full dry run at home. Discovering a seized nut or a missing locking key on the hard shoulder is the worst version of this.
proof: You change a wheel unaided in your driveway in under twenty minutes, torqued correctly.
